briefdescription.para: Explicit Configurator::get<T>() specializations that expose each configuration section.

detaileddescription.para: The Configurator class declares a generic get<T>() accessor but does not define its behaviour for any particular type. This file supplies one explicit specialization per configuration section. Each one simply returns the matching private member stored in the Configurator object. In plain words: this file is the lookup table that maps a type name, such as ServerConfig, to the actual settings object of that type held by the Configurator.

WHY THIS FILE MATTERS IN THE SERVER: Code throughout the server asks for its settings by type, for example store.config().get<Configurator::ServerConfig>(). Those calls only link successfully because this file defines each specialization. Without it, the compiler accepts the calls but the linker reports undefined references, so the server cannot obtain any of its configuration sections at runtime. Keeping the definitions here (not in the header) also means adding a new section requires updating this single mapping.

CONCEPTS TO LEARN (for beginners):
C++ concepts and constraints: https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/constraints
Explicit (full) template specialization: https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/template_specialization
Function templates: https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/function_template
